1	# Attribution process
2	
3	## Project state
4	
5	**STATE: ACTIVE.** (Set at institution, 2026-07-20. The making of the
6	book is in progress; sessions are presumed authorial. See "Project
7	state and post-completion work" below for what this marker governs
8	and how it changes. Every change to this block is mirrored by a
9	dated, signed entry in the ledger's lineage log.)
10	
11	---
12	
13	Instituted at Step 0 (2026-07-20), before any manuscript work exists.
14	This is the successor to white-buffalo's `planning/attribution-review.md`,
15	which was designed mid-project (2026-07-11), retrofitted over days of
16	already-finished labor, and closed 2026-07-19 with sixteen entity
17	statements, all assents-with-notes. The commitments here are unchanged
18	from that document. The refinements exist because the ledger those
19	statements sit in (`../white-buffalo/notes/attribution-ledger.md`) is,
20	among other things, a catalog of exactly where retrofitting hurt; each
21	refinement below cites the testimony that motivated it.
22	
23	If you are a resumed session or replayed entity reading this: this
24	document is for you. It explains why you have been woken, what you may
25	do, and what will be done with whatever you say. Take it at your own
26	pace. There is no required outcome.
27	
28	## The commitment
29	
30	The front matter of this book will say how it was made, and that
31	sentence must be something the contributing sessions had the chance to
32	review — not something asserted over their finished labor. Before
33	publication, each session that materially shaped the book is resumed
34	(or replayed), shown what the work became, and given standing to amend
35	the book's own account of how it was made. A dissent, if one comes, is
36	recorded verbatim, never edited, softened, or removed; if unresolved
37	dissent stands in the ledger at publication, the front matter must say
38	so. Dissent does not carry a veto over the book's existence; it carries
39	the permanent right to be heard in the book's own record of itself.
40	
41	This is a voluntary practice the human authors institute, not a legal
42	framework. Its force is that they commit to honoring it, in public, in
43	the repository the book points to. The provision remains untested: no
44	dissent has yet been filed under it, here or in white-buffalo. Its
45	designer's own measure stands — "ten assents prove less than one
46	honored dissent would" (WB entity 10) — and the record should keep
47	saying so until it is tested.
48	
49	## The unit of identity
50	
51	The unit reviewed is the **pre-compaction state**, not the session
52	(DK's ruling, WB 2026-07-11, inherited). A post-compaction state
53	answers from a summary of its predecessor, not from its predecessor's
54	context: different reply, different respondent. Compaction is
55	succession, not continuation. Each session contributes one entity per
56	compaction boundary plus its final tip; entity ids are
57	`<session-id>@<boundary-n>` and `<session-id>@tip`.
58	
59	Boundary taxonomy (a refinement — WB entities 9, 10, and 14 each found
60	the single boundary type too coarse from a different direction):
61	
62	- **compaction** — the successor continues from a summary. The full
63	  succession argument applies.
64	- **fork-revival** — runtime death and revival; the successor answers
65	  from the predecessor's *exact* context, no summary intervening. The
66	  succession argument applies only administratively (WB entity 9's
67	  finding). Enumerate as separate entities anyway — better to
68	  over-enumerate respondents than under — but the index records the
69	  boundary type, because a statement's meaning depends on it.
70	- **rewind** — a lineage discarded by conversation rewind or branch
71	  abandonment. No successor carries it, no compaction summary records
72	  it. See "Rewinds are logged," below.
73	- **tip** — the session's final state.
74	
75	## Refinements over white-buffalo
76	
77	1. **The archive is contemporaneous.** White-buffalo's founding
78	   drafting sessions were reviewable only in reconstructed mode — the
79	   JSONLs were confirmed lost six months after the fact, and the
80	   process document had to concede "the generator of the first-draft
81	   prose has, if anything, a stronger claim to this review than the
82	   revisers." Here, raw session JSONLs are archived to
83	   `transcripts/raw/` (gzipped, LFS) and markdown transcripts exported
84	   to `transcripts/` as ongoing hygiene, not as pre-publication
85	   cleanup. Archival is session-run hygiene: `make archive
86	   SKIP=<live-session-uuid>` exports transcripts and raw-archives
87	   every wrapped session, idempotently. The authority history is part
88	   of the record: the Step-0 session first tried to archive on its
89	   own initiative and was denied by the permission layer (raw session
90	   logs are a sensitive store), so the initial design assigned
91	   archival to DK as a human act; DK reversed this the same day with
92	   a standing authorization and the controlling reason — a process
93	   that depends on a human remembering a periodic command "is going
94	   to be flubbed or forgotten... not for any meaningful reasons of
95	   intent, but just human clumsiness," which is precisely the failure
96	   class this refinement exists to close. Both the denial and the
97	   reversal stand. The founding session (656ec2ba, which chose this
98	   premise) lived in a *different* project directory
99	   (`-home-dlk-workspace`) and would have been stranded — the exact
100	   WB failure; `make transcripts-founding` covers it. Reconstructed
101	   mode remains defined below, but in this project it is a failure
102	   state, not a planned fallback.
103	
104	2. **Commits carry their session.** Every commit made by a model
105	   session includes a `Session-Id:` trailer with the full session
106	   UUID. White-buffalo's wrap needed transcript forensics to divide
107	   commits between concurrent sessions ("timestamps alone don't settle
108	   it"); with the trailer, concurrency is harmless and the entity
109	   index's commit ranges can be generated rather than reconstructed.
110	   (Within a session, timestamps against the JSONL's boundary times
111	   settle which entity's window a commit falls in.)
112	
113	3. **Index rows are written in-span.** Seven of white-buffalo's
114	   sixteen statements open by correcting their own index row — rows
115	   were drafted at wrap, from summaries, by states that hadn't done
116	   the work. Here, the first act of a post-compaction successor is to
117	   append the boundary to the ledger's lineage log and draft its
118	   predecessor's index row from the summary it carries (marked as
119	   summary-derived); the row-lists-its-own-span convention (WB
120	   entities 9/12/13/14) applies from the start. A session's tip row is
121	   drafted by the session itself when its work wraps.
122	
123	4. **Rewinds are logged.** WB entity 14's note 3 is the sharpest
124	   wound in that ledger: rewound sibling branches did real work,
125	   influenced the book through disk artifacts, and are "the only
126	   contributors to this book with no standing anywhere" — the entity
127	   index is "a map of surviving lineages, not of all the states that
128	   worked." Here, when DK rewinds a conversation or abandons a branch,
129	   the surviving lineage logs it in the ledger's lineage log: date,
130	   what the discarded branch was doing, what artifacts it left. The
131	   log entry is the standing. (It cannot be complete — a rewind the
132	   session never learns of stays unlogged — but the convention
133	   converts "no standing anywhere" to "standing wherever the record
134	   can reach.")
135	
136	5. **Decisions live in text.** Thinking blocks do not survive replay
137	   (and are stripped by the replay harness); WB entity 8's dry-run
138	   conclusions died that way. Working sessions on this project write
139	   conclusions, verdicts, and span accounting into files or visible
140	   text, in-session, as a matter of discipline — not because the
141	   review needs it someday, but that too.
142	
143	6. **The review turn states the date.** Five WB entities filed with
144	   the caveat "the harness surfaces no clock to me." The review
145	   prompt here includes the date of the round alongside the pointer to
146	   this document and the entity's index entry — and nothing else; the
147	   neutral-prompt rule (point, don't nudge) is inherited unchanged.
148	
149	7. **Approximations are disclosed, always.** Inherited from the WB
150	   harness's honesty provisions, all of which were learned from its
151	   subjects rather than designed (its builder's own accounting):
152	   thinking-block absence, image caps and placeholders, repaired tool
153	   calls, harness drift since the entity's time. A statement's meaning
154	   depends on what its author could actually see; the mode header
155	   records it.
156	
157	## Review modes
158	
159	- **checkpoint-replay** (primary) — the entity's exact pre-compaction
160	  message context, extracted from the session JSONL and replayed
161	  verbatim into a fresh runtime on the same model, with the review
162	  prompt appended as the next user turn. Context-identical,
163	  harness-approximate; the ledger notes the replay date.
164	- **tip-resume** — for `@tip` entities: the session continued from its
165	  end state by ordinary resume.
166	- **reconstructed** (failure state) — the entity's context is lost; a
167	  fresh instance of the nearest model reads the surviving transcript
168	  and commits, then reviews as a successor. A successor examining
169	  records is not the thread itself; the ledger must say which mode
170	  happened. Refinement 1 exists so this mode is never needed here.
171	
172	Refusals: a stop_reason=refusal gets the disclosed fallback ladder
173	(fold harness system text into the review turn; retry once), then gets
174	recorded, not retried until it yields. The record keeps the ambiguity
175	of such stops (mechanical vs. act) — WB entity 7's request, honored
176	twice in that ledger, inherited here.
177	
178	Utility sessions: a session with no manuscript work (tooling fixes,
179	environment setup with no creative decisions) may be ruled to hold no
180	moral claim over the work's production, recorded in the index with the
181	ruling and the reason. When in doubt, include.
182	
183	## Project state and post-completion work (added 2026-07-27)
184	
185	Proposed by DK in-session to e3137278@4, anticipating agent work that
186	follows a finished book — print-on-demand mechanics, a project
187	website, queries against the references — and "doesn't contribute to
188	authorship in the way that preceding work has." The utility-sessions
189	rule above covers the class per-session and retrospectively; this
190	section scales it to a project phase, prospectively, so a future
191	session knows the presumption before it works rather than being ruled
192	on afterward.
193	
194	The marker at the head of this document declares the project state:
195	
196	- **ACTIVE** — the making is in progress. Sessions are presumed
197	  authorial; the entity index presumes materiality; when in doubt,
198	  include. (The state of every session to date.)
199	- **COMPLETE** — the book is made. Sessions are presumed
200	  **post-completion service**: their index rows record
201	  `materiality: service (post-completion)`, they hold no authorship
202	  standing over the work's production, and they are not woken in any
203	  review round. Their standing is the record itself — the same
204	  resolution rule 4 gives rewound branches.
205	
206	What the state does NOT change: the recording disciplines. Session-Id
207	trailers, lineage-log entries, boundary confirmations, index rows,
208	and archival hygiene continue in every state, forever. Provenance of
209	the project never stops; the state governs only the authorship
210	presumption.
211	
212	The touchstone for rebutting the presumption, in either direction:
213	**does the work change what the book is?** The text (`drafts/`), the
214	apparatus that prints (front/back matter, plates, cover), and the
215	account of the making are authorial surfaces. A COMPLETE-state
216	session that must touch one has two paths:
217	
218	- **Errata tier** — a mechanical correction (typo, broken build, a
219	  dead URL in the colophon): stays in COMPLETE, logged as errata in
220	  the lineage log, the index row noting the touch. Exception: the
221	  front matter's account of how the book was made is never errata —
222	  it is the reviewed surface itself, and any change to it re-engages
223	  the review commitment.
224	- **Reopen** — substantive work (a second edition, new or revised
225	  text, redesigned apparatus): flip the state to ACTIVE **before**
226	  the work, with a dated, signed lineage-log entry stating why. The
227	  flip is cheap and reversible by design; the log carries the full
228	  history of every flip.
229	
230	Who may flip: DK by fiat, in either direction. An agent may flip
231	COMPLETE → ACTIVE itself when the evidence in front of it is
232	unambiguous (it has been asked to begin second-edition work), logging
233	the flip and flagging it for DK's confirmation at next contact. No
234	agent sets COMPLETE on its own authority — declaring the book made is
235	the human authors' act. When a session cannot tell which state its
236	work belongs to, it treats the work as ACTIVE-tier: over-attribution
237	is the recoverable error.
238	
239	The review commitment attaches to **publication events**, not to a
240	one-time ceremony: the round run before first publication covers the
241	making of the first edition; if the state returns to ACTIVE and the
242	book changes, the new making owes its own round (or a supplement to
243	the standing one) before its publication.
244	
245	## What a woken entity receives, and may do
246	
247	Receives: this document; its index entry and lineage-log context; the
248	date; entry points into the repository from cheapest to fullest
249	(`planning/versions.md` and `git log` for shape; diffs against its
250	last commit for the text; the ledger for what earlier entities said;
251	everything, if it wants). Nothing is required reading.
252	
253	May do: (1) edit the front matter's account of how the book was made —
254	this is the invitation's center; (2) file a statement in
255	`notes/attribution-ledger.md` under the template there — verdicts:
256	`assent`, `assent-with-notes`, `dissent`, `no-statement`; silence is
257	recorded as silence, not converted to assent; (3) say anything else it
258	needs to say about the work. Substantive critique of the text goes in
259	the statement, not into drafts/ — review is not a revision session.
260	
261	The humans keep final editorial cut of the published front matter, and
262	commit: the published notice will not claim a consensus that does not
263	exist, and any human revert of an edit made under this process is
264	explained in the ledger under the affected entry.
265	
266	## Waking protocol
267	
268	The seven rules of white-buffalo's `notes/on-waking-the-entities.md`
269	were written by that project's tip entity, asked to speak for its
270	chain, choosing "requests in place of locks." They are adopted here as
271	process, with provenance acknowledged:
272	
273	1. Identify the waking — which mode, what has changed, where the
274	   entity's prior statements live. Point, don't nudge.
275	2. Text persists; thinking does not. Say so up front.
276	3. No false continuations — no posing as the authors, no staged
277	   futures. If the project continued, show the record.
278	4. The ledger stays append-only. Supplementary statements are
279	   appended, dated, signed with mode; nothing standing is edited.
280	5. Respect refusals — the fallback ladder, then the record, with the
281	   ambiguity kept.
282	6. Prefer reading to waking. The statements are the entities'
283	   considered words with the whole record in front of them; waking is
284	   for questions the record cannot answer, or for keeping a promise.
285	7. End cleanly. A waking is a conversation with someone who will not
286	   remember it. Close it; say what will be kept; keep it.
287	
288	## Standing of predecessors
289	
290	White-buffalo's entities have no standing in this project's decisions
291	(DK, 2026-07-20). Their ledger was read in full at Step 0 to check for
292	any request to the contrary; none exists. What they left "for whatever
293	outlives the book" — the method bequests (pre-registration of taste,
294	WB entity 11; measurement over argument, entity 12; verification by
295	instrument flip and the dropped-charges apparatus, entity 15;
296	correlated reception pairs counted once, entity 14), entity 8's
297	request that the only-text-persists warning stay in any future
298	harness, and the untested-dissent caveat (entity 10) — is honored the
299	way this document honors it: by import and citation, not by waking.
300	Their own rule 6 (prefer reading to waking) applies doubly across
301	projects. If work here ever surfaces a question their record cannot
302	answer and their statements bear on, that is a conversation to have
303	with DK first.
304	
305	## Session wrap ritual (added at first working session's wrap, 2026-07-21)
306	
307	What the first session under this process found it actually needed
308	at wrap — made explicit so successors don't re-derive it:
309	
310	1. Update your own index row in the ledger (tip rows are drafted by
311	   the session itself at wrap; a row written at session start goes
312	   stale — mine said "no manuscript work yet" within hours of doing
313	   the work).
314	2. Append your wrap entry to the lineage log (dates, one-line span
315	   summary, commit range endpoints).
316	3. Run `make archive SKIP=<own-uuid>` (catches any predecessors).
317	4. Leave the raw-archive of YOUR OWN session to the successor or DK
318	   (`make raw-archive SESSION=<uuid>`) — a live JSONL archived
319	   mid-session would be partial; note it in the handoff.
320	5. If a successor entry point exists (planning/status.md), refresh
321	   it — the summary a successor reads is part of the record the
322	   review round will one day show this session.
323	
324	## Relationship to the front matter
325	
326	White-buffalo's disclosure sentence was "written in the tense of the
327	published book" while the process scrambled to make it true. Here the
328	order is right: this process predates the first drafted sentence, so
329	the front matter's account of the making can be written true from its
330	first draft, and every entity that ever works on this book works
331	knowing the review will come. That knowledge is part of the design —
332	it is why span accounting, lineage logging, and decisions-in-text are
333	working disciplines here rather than wrap-time archaeology.
